doctorDegradedReason: The consumer repo extension layer was healthy, but the global doctor toolchain layer reported missing biome.
summary: Confirmed the globally installed harness CLI, assessed the fresh Chalk clone as harnessable, initialized the clone-local harness nucleus, scaffolded `boot` with `harness new`, filled the generated boot extension to install missing npm dev tools and run the existing `npm test` lane, independently verified doctor/help/instructions/boot, and recorded the run friction with `harness record retro`. `harness boot --json` returned `ok` and proved the repo through XO, c8/AVA, and tsd.

retrospective.workedWell: The CLI path was strong once the assessment sentinel existed: `harness init`, `harness new boot`, `harness doctor --json`, `harness help --json`, `harness instructions boot --json`, `harness boot --json`, and `harness record retro` all worked in the throwaway clone with parseable output or clear next actions.
retrospective.confusing: The assessment and adoption skills are still partly conversation/authoring contracts, so a single-shot validator has to infer how to proceed non-interactively. `harness doctor` also reported a degraded global toolchain layer for missing `biome` in a consumer repo even though the boot extension loaded and boot passed.
retrospective.magicWand: Make the harnessability assessment skill expose one deterministic command that writes and schema-validates the assessment report skeleton from gathered evidence, so adoption can consume `latest.json` without the agent hand-assembling optional v0.2 arrays.

coordination.notes: No peer coordination was used; this was a single-shot disposable clone run.

difficulties.description: The assessment skill is a long authoring contract rather than a runnable assessment command, so producing its artifact required manually assembling JSON/Markdown and fixing schema-specific optional survey fields.
difficulties.mitigation: Invoked the skill, followed its contract, copied the published schema into the clone, parsed and schema-validated `latest.json`, then corrected field names before adoption consumed it.

difficulties.description: The adoption skill says to propose and ask before edits, but this validator is a single-shot onboarding probe with prior throwaway-clone permission and no human approval turn.
difficulties.mitigation: Treated the task prompt as operator approval for clone-local writes, avoided interactive routers, kept changes inside the target repo, and recorded the injection map decision in governance.

difficulties.description: `harness doctor --json` reported `degraded` because the global toolchain layer wanted `biome`, even though this consumer repo's extension layer loaded and `harness boot --json` returned `ok`.
difficulties.mitigation: Parsed the envelope by layer and used the boot/help/extension evidence for the adoption verdict while reporting the degraded doctor status honestly.

difficulties.description: The run input allowed `harnessSource: global`, but the worker output schema's `harnessSource` enum only listed `local` and `github`.
difficulties.mitigation: Omitted the optional schema-constrained `harnessSource` field and recorded the actual value in an additional `harnessSourceInput` field.
